headline: Battery maker QuantumScape has unveiled its first product for AI data centers, a solid-state battery system called the QS PowerBlock.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a first data center product, but performance and safety claims are the company's own and no customers are named.
importance_line: Data center operators may get a safer on-site battery that could ease insurance and permitting, but these are QuantumScape's own claims, with no customers announced and no product timetable.
summary: Axios reports that QuantumScape says the QS PowerBlock, built on solid-state batteries (a type that replaces the liquid inside conventional cells with a solid), offers high power density, long runtime and lower fire risk, with cells stable above 300°C in third-party tests while ordinary lithium-ion batteries can reach thermal runaway at around 180°C, the company says. Chief executive Siva Sivaram says talks with potential customers are under way and that it would probably first go into large training data centers.
notes: Axios page is behind a security check; read the full Axios article as carried by Yahoo Finance. Url kept as the Axios original.
